label: rem:canonical-trace-factorises-over-chain
title: The canonical mass trace factorises over the chain: the bond constants are $-\log(z+d)$ and the canonical closure carries no many-body binding
html:
Remark. The canonical mass trace factorises over the chain: the bond constants are -\log(z+d) and the canonical closure carries no many-body binding

The chain form has an algebraic consequence that is stronger than the topological one. Write the canonical Hecke word as \prod_i p_i(\sigma_i), one polynomial per generator in Coxeter order -- the averaged letters sit inside the power of their own generator, so this needs no branch to be chosen. Then the normalised Markov trace on H_{3A} is the product of two-strand traces,

  \mathrm{tr}_M\Bigl(\prod_i p_i(\sigma_i)\Bigr)
  \;=\;
  \prod_i \bigl[\,w_+\,p_i(q) + w_-\,p_i(-q^{-1})\,\bigr],
  \qquad
  w_+ = \frac{[3]_q}{[3]_q+1},\quad w_- = \frac{1}{[3]_q+1},

because a closed braid whose word is a product of sub-words on strand sets overlapping in one strand is a connected sum, and the Markov trace -- like every multiplicative link invariant -- is multiplicative under connected sum, not only under the split union of the KS shortcut. Each interface generator carries the single letter \sigma + d, whose two-strand trace is

  w_+(q + d) + w_-(-q^{-1} + d) \;=\; z + d,
  \qquad z = \frac{q^3}{q^2+1},

so the free-minus-atom log-ratio is exactly a sum over the A-1 interfaces:

  L(Z,N) \;=\; \sum_{\text{interfaces}} -\log(z + d_i),
  \qquad
  L_{pp} = -\log z,\quad
  L_{nn} = -\log(z - h) = \log\bigl(q(q^2+1)\bigr),\quad
  L_{pn} = -\log(z + d_{pn}).

Measured

At 200 bits, with q from the fifty-digit substrate value, the full H_{3A} Markov trace of the canonical word against the product of two-strand factors: ^2H (n=6) 2.3\times10^{-59}, ^3H and ^3He (n=9) 3.1\times10^{-59}, ^4He (n=12) 4.0\times10^{-59}; the Jones polynomial of the closure equals \prod_i V(T(2,e_i)) exactly on both classical branches for A \le 4. The three constants -\log(z+d) reproduce the binding arc's bond constants -- measured there in H_6 -- to all sixty digits (the_canonical_mass_trace_factorises_over_the_chain_probe.py).

What it means for the binding gap

The linear-chain closed form B_{\mathrm{sym}} = a\,[(Z-1)L_{pp} + L_{pn} + (N-1)L_{nn}], which the Lean formalisation of that result took as its named structural input, is a corollary of the topology: connected sum \Rightarrow multiplicative trace \Rightarrow additive L. The canonical closure therefore carries no many-body binding at all -- not by measurement, by theorem. The many-body cumulants the binding arc found (c_3 < 0, c_4 < 0, c_5 > 0, the order-six datum) belong to the all-pairs bond model, whose band-routed bonds interleave generators across blocks and destroy the chain form. With \alpha = m_e/(q_0(q_0-1)) = 4.185981 MeV the chain gives ^4He 8.6817 MeV against B_{\mathrm{AME}} = 28.2957, namely 31\,\%; the missing 69\,\% is absent from the canonical closure because a connected sum has nothing to put there. Any closure that carries genuinely many-body binding must fail to be composite -- non-split, prime, with the kind of irreducibly multi-component linking the Borromean rings have and this chain does not. That is the precise form of "the missing binding is not in the bond graph", and it says which topology the search has to move to.

The affine law also disposes of the obvious repair. Any modification acting as an interface offset -- a convention change, a fractional twist insertion q^{2c(\lambda)/n} -- has bond constant -\log(z+d) with no trace to run, so invert it: closing ^4He on the chain with a common offset needs -\log(z+d) = 2.253212, i.e. d = -0.507627 = -2.4281\,h. The algebra's letters supply d \in \{0, -h/2, d_{pn}, -h\}, so d/h \in [-1, 0]: the required offset is 2.43\times more negative than the most negative letter that exists. No interface offset can close the gap.

The quantity L itself is a free-energy difference over the Markov state sum; that it is the binding energy is a separate and open claim, recorded in the free-energy reading.

The stated form assumes the grouped intra ordering; the conclusion does not

Writing the word as \prod_i p_i(\sigma_i) — one polynomial per generator — requires each generator's letters to be contiguous. That is a property of how the word is assembled, not of the chain topology. The corpus's live builder atom_braid_word_3A does assemble it that way (all of the \sigma_0 chain, then all of the \sigma_1 chain), which is why the identity measures exact above. Since 2026-09-05 the live builder instead lays each nucleon's six confinement letters down alternating, as the (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 its own source comment always named — the Borromean braid \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}}, identified against its Lean closed form to 5\times10^{-60}. Same letter multiset, different order, and it does not satisfy the per-generator form: that fails by 2.8\times at A = 2, rising to 13.3\times at A = 4.

A distinction worth keeping, because this arc's bean once lost it. Grouped and alternating describe the arrangement of six letters inside the eleven-letter intra block, not the block itself. That block is not \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} under either arrangement and cannot be: two of its eleven letters are averaged, \sigma - (h/2)\cdot 1, which is outside the image of \rho : B_n \to H_n(q), so it is not a braid at all and has no single closure to name. One proton: 1.145759692457300870 grouped, 0.629328402202921918 alternating, against 0.998562163836787266 for the bare six-letter \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} — three distinct objects.

Nothing above is retracted by that. The load-bearing step is connected-sum multiplicativity, which is blind to letter order inside a summand, and it is measured to survive the reordering exactly: \mathrm{tr}_M(\text{chain}) = \prod_k \mathrm{tr}_M(\text{intra}_k)\prod_i(z+d_i). So the interface factors, the three bond constants and L itself are identical under both orderings — to \sim 10^{-60} at A = 2, 3, 4 — and the "no many-body binding" conclusion holds for either word. What is ordering-specific is the stronger per-generator statement.

The same caveat applies one level up, to the chain form: "every generator occurs in exactly one contiguous run", so that the closure is a linear connected sum of (2,k) torus links, is again a property of the assembly. With the confinement core alternating, a nucleon's letters no longer form two runs, so that reading of the block lapses. It is tempting to go further and say the block therefore satisfies this arc's own criterion for where many-body binding could live — "a closure that fails to be composite, non-split, prime, with the kind of irreducibly multi-component linking the Borromean rings have" — but that would be unsupported twice over: the block is a weighted sum of branch closures rather than one link, and containing \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} as a subword is not the same as being prime. What is actually measured is only that L is unchanged to \sim 10^{-60}: the reordering happens inside each nucleon, the nucleons remain strung on a chain, and no many-body binding appears anywhere.

What moves is every absolute trace: the intra factor falls by 3.8\times at ^2H to 14.3\times at ^4He when the confinement core is relaid alternating, carrying the difference-based B = Q_\beta\bigl(\mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{free}}) - \mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{atom}})\bigr) route with it by the same factor.

QOU.Mass.IntraOrderingInvariance (sorry-free) proves the split. Given the connected-sum input — \mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{atom}}) = F \prod_i (z + d_i) and \mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\text{free}}) = F — the ratio is \prod_i (z+d_i) for any intra factor F \neq 0, so two orderings with factors F_1, F_2 give the same ratio with no hypothesis relating them (chainRatio_eq_of_intra), and hence the same L (L_chain_indep_of_intra, L_chain_eq_sum_of_intra). The invariance is cancellation, not coincidence. The difference route instead satisfies F_1(1-P) = (F_1/F_2)\,F_2(1-P) (chainDiff_scales) and genuinely differs whenever F_1 \neq F_2 and P \neq 1 (chainDiff_ne). And the two confinement words are different objects: at q = 1, where both are elementary, the per-generator product is 1/4 and the Borromean closed form is 1 (grouped_ne_borromean), so the 82\,\% gap at q_0 is not a deformation artefact. Not formalised, as ever, is the connected-sum multiplicativity itself. Measured in the_intra_ordering_moves_absolute_traces_not_the_bond_model_probe.py; which word is \beta_{\mathrm{Bor}} is measured in nf_vs_canonical_word_order_probe.py.

What is formalised, what is checked, what is cited

QOU.Mass.ChainTraceFactor (sorry-free) proves the factor algebra: the affine law \mathrm{tr}_2(\sigma + d) = z + d from the level-2 Wenzl weights (twoStrandTrace_eq); the mirror factor z - h = 1/(q(q^2+1)) and \mathrm{tr}_2(\sigma)\,\mathrm{tr}_2(\sigma^{-1}) = 1/[2]_q^2, hence L_{pp} + L_{nn} = 2\log(q + q^{-1}); positivity of all three factors for q \ge 1; and that -\log of a product of positive factors is the sum of the -\logs. The factorisation of the H_{3A} trace is checked at A \le 4 and rests on the chain form (verified through A = 12) plus the connected-sum multiplicativity of the Markov trace, which is classical [birman1974] and not formalised. Nothing here says which prime closure would carry many-body binding, or that one exists in the framework.
